about.title: Manhattan Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't ask permission before it fails — a faulty bike component on the Strand, a malfunctioning kitchen appliance in a Manhattan Beach kitchen, or a poorly designed piece of sports gear used along Sepulveda Boulevard or near the pier can turn an ordinary afternoon into an emergency room visit. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person often doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That can mean a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing or inadequate warning. Multiple parties along the supply chain — the manufacturer, a distributor, or the retailer — may share responsibility. If you were hurt by a product in Manhattan Beach, keeping the item itself, along with packaging, receipts, and any manuals, can matter a great deal later. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect you, at no cost, to an independent attorney in our network who can review what happened and explain your options.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near the Manhattan Beach pier — what should I do with it?
items.answer: Try to preserve the product exactly as it was when it failed, including any packaging, parts, or manuals. This physical evidence is often central to a product liability claim, since an attorney or expert may need to examine it. Avoid attempting repairs or discarding any broken pieces.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims frequently rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on proving carelessness. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this might apply.
